questions.question: To test for possible anterior shoulder instability a physical therapist should move the humerus into:
questions.explanation: Anterior instability is tested with abduction and lateral rotation (apprehension test).
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient is referred to physical therapy with a C6 nerve root injury. Which of the following clinical findings would not be expected with this type of injury?

options.A: Diminished sensation on the anterior arm and the index finger
options.B: Weakness in the biceps and supinator
options.D: Paresthesias of the long and ring fingers

questions.explanation: C6 root lesions affect thumb and index sensation; paraesthesia of the middle and ring fingers is C7-C8.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist is concerned about the possibility of a patient developing a deep vein thrombosis following surgery. Which of the following special test would be useful to identify the presence of a deep vein thrombosis?
questions.explanation: Homans' sign (calf pain on dorsiflexion) is the traditional sign for deep vein thrombosis.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: While examining a patient diagnosed with Achilles tendonitis, a therapist, notes that the foot appears to be pronated in standing. Which motions combine to create pronation?
questions.explanation: Pronation combines abduction, dorsiflexion and eversion.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist examines a patient with bicipital tendonitis. Which clinical finding would you not expect the therapist to identify when examining the patient?

options.A: Isometric resistance to the biceps brachii increases subjective pain levels
options.B: Referred pain in the c7-c8 dermatome
options.C: A painful arc is noted with active range of motion of the involved shoulder
options.D: Tenderness to palpation over the bicipital tendon

questions.explanation: Bicipital tendinitis does not usually refer pain to the C7-C8 dermatome.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Essential of Orthopaedics & Applied Physiotherapy Jayant Joshi/1st Ed./Pg. 483

questions.question: A physical therapist examines a 16-year-old male diag- nosed with left knee anterior cruciate ligament insufficiency. During the examination a Lachman test is performed. Ideally, the therapist should perform the test with the knee in:
questions.explanation: The Lachman test is performed at about 25 to 35 degrees of knee flexion.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist examines a patient referred to physical therapy diagnosed with bicipital tendonitis. Which of the following special tests would be the most useful to confirm the patient's diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Yergason's test (resisted supination) confirms bicipital tendinitis.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Orthopaedic Physical Assessment/5th Ed./Pg. 309

questions.question: A physical therapist is concerned with a patient's lateral knee discomfort. The therapist attempts to determine if contracture tensor fasciae latae or iliotibial band could be contributing to the patient's symptoms. Which special test might help to identify a restriction in this area? Exercise Therapy 11
questions.explanation: Ober's test detects tensor fasciae latae and iliotibial band tightness.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Essential of Orthopaedics & Applied Physiotherapy/ Jayant Joshi/5th Ed./Pg. 693-694

questions.question: A therapist hypothesizes that patient's persistent shoulder pain is caused by an injury to a specific upper extremity muscle. What selective tissue tension assessment would provide the therapist with the most useful information to test the hypothesis?
questions.explanation: Resisted isometric testing implicates the contractile structure when strong and painful.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist attempts to gain information on the ligamentous integrity of the knee. Which of the following special tests would not provide the therapist with the desired information?
questions.explanation: The apprehension test assesses patellar instability, not ligament integrity.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist performs a talar tilt test on a 22-year-old female rehabilitating from an inversion ankle sprain. Which ligament does the talar tilt test examine?
questions.explanation: The talar tilt test (inversion stress) tests the calcaneofibular ligament.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient rehabilitating from knee surgery is examined in physical therapy. The patient's involved knee range of motion begins at 15 degrees of flexion and ends at 90 degrees of flexion. The total available range of motion for this patient is _______degrees?
questions.explanation: Total arc is 90 minus 15, which is 75 degrees.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient is able to actively hyperextend the right knee 5 degrees. Assuming the patient's total knee range of motion is 65 degrees, which of the following recordings would be the most representative of the patient's actual range of motion?
questions.explanation: Hyperextension is recorded first: 5-0-60.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: McMurray's test is most frequently positive in which of the following injuries?
questions.explanation: McMurray's test is positive most often in medial meniscus tears.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Bryant's triangle is useful in diagnosis of following except:
questions.explanation: Bryant's triangle detects supratrochanteric shortening, not intratrochanteric.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient with recurrent dislocation of shoulder presents to the hospital. The doctor tries to abduct his arm and to extend the elbow and external rotation, but the patient doesn't allow to do so. This test is called:
questions.explanation: Resistance to abduction with external rotation in recurrent dislocation is the apprehension test.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Best diagnostic procedure for ACL injury
questions.explanation: The Lachman test is the most reliable test for ACL injury.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist attempts to obtain information on the ability of noncontractile tissue to allow motion at a specific joint. Which selective tissue tension assessment would provide the therapist with the most valuable information?
questions.explanation: Passive range of motion tests the non-contractile tissues.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist completes a selected resistive test as part of an initial examination. The patient reports feeling pain during the test, however strength is normal. Which of the following conclusions is most likely?

options.B: A minor lesion of the muscle or tendon
options.C: A complete rupture of the muscle or tendon

questions.explanation: Painful but strong resisted movement suggests a minor muscle or tendon lesion.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Thomas knee flexion test is used to detect:
questions.explanation: The Thomas test detects hip flexion deformity.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Thomas test is done for identifying which deformity?
questions.explanation: The Thomas test identifies a fixed flexion deformity of the hip.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Modified Allen's test is used for:
questions.explanation: The modified Allen's test assesses radial (and ulnar) artery patency.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Positive Froment's test suggests involvement of which nerve?
questions.explanation: A positive Froment's sign indicates ulnar nerve palsy.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Purpose of the heel knee test is to

options.D: Assesses coordination of movement of lower extremities

questions.explanation: The heel-to-knee (heel-shin) test assesses coordination of the lower limbs.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist attempts to assess the integrity of the L4 spinal level. Which deep tendon reflex would provide the therapist with the most useful information?
questions.explanation: The patellar reflex tests the L4 level.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist performs a manual muscle test on a patient with unilateral lower extremity weakness. The therapist should test the patient's hip adductors with the patient positioned in:
questions.explanation: Hip adductors are tested in side-lying with the test leg supported or the opposite leg lifted.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist instructs a patient to close her eyes and hold out her hand. The therapist places a series of different weights in the patient's hand one at a time. The patient is then asked to identify the comparative weight of the objects. This method of sensory testing is used to examine:
questions.explanation: Identifying differences in weights placed in the hand tests barognosis.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist attempts to have a patient quantify his pain using a subjective pain scale. The therapist explains to the patient that he should assign a numerical value between zero and ten to describe the pain. Which of the following would best describe a score of ten?
questions.explanation: On a 0-10 scale a score of 10 means the worst pain imaginable.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist attempts to gather information on the ligamentous integrity of a patient's knee. Which special test would be inappropriate based on the desired objective?
questions.explanation: McMurray's test is for the meniscus, not ligamentous integrity.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Essential Orthopaedics/Maheswari Mehta/3rd Ed./Pg. 313

questions.question: A therapist identifies signs and symptoms of neurovascular compression after examining a patient with an upper extremity injury. Which of the following special tests would not be helpful in identifying the presence of neurovascular compression?
questions.explanation: The Bunnell-Littler test assesses intrinsic muscle tightness, not neurovascular compression.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist attempts to measure a patient's shoulder lateral rotation. Proper positioning the upper extremity in supine would be described by which of the following?

options.A: Shoulder abducted to 90 degrees, elbow flexed to 90 degrees
options.B: Shoulder abducted to 90 degrees, elbow fully extended
options.C: Shoulder abducted to 90 degrees, elbow flexed to 45 degrees
options.D: Shoulder in neutral, elbow flexed to 90 degrees

questions.explanation: Shoulder lateral rotation is measured supine with the arm abducted 90 degrees and elbow flexed 90 degrees.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist can obtain valuable information during an examination by using special orthopedic tests. Which of the following tests in not performed with the patient in supine?
questions.explanation: Apley's compression test is performed in prone; the others are done supine.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Ober test is used to test contracture of the:
questions.explanation: Ober's test assesses tightness of the iliotibial band.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Which test is concerned with tennis elbow?
questions.explanation: Cozen's test (resisted wrist extension) is used for tennis elbow.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter:
Cited reference: Essential of Orthopaedics & Applied Physiotherapy/

Maheshwari/3rd Ed./Pg. 313

questions.question: A therapist examines a patient referred to physical therapy with thoracic outlet syndrome. Which of the following special tests would not assist the therapist to confirm the physician's diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Speed's manoeuvre tests the biceps tendon, not thoracic outlet compression.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: McMurray's test is performed to clinically identify:
questions.explanation: McMurray's test identifies meniscal tears.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Duga's test is helpful in:
questions.explanation: Duga's test (hand to opposite shoulder) helps diagnose anterior dislocation of the shoulder.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Phalan's test is positive in:
questions.explanation: Phalen's test is positive in carpal tunnel syndrome.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Essential of Orthopaedics & Applied Physiotherapy/ Jayant Joshi/Elesiver/1st Ed./Pg. 265

questions.question: Patient with pain in cervical region, is immediately refered from physical therapy department to a higher orthopedic specialty center. Possibly which of following test was found positive by therapist during assessment? Exercise Therapy 29
questions.explanation: A positive Sharp-Purser test indicates atlantoaxial instability and needs urgent specialist referral.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: What is maitland's 2nd degree of mobilization:

options.A: Large amplitude of movement performed up to limit of range
options.B: Small amplitude of movement performed up to limit of range
options.C: Large amplitude of movement performed within the free range but not moving into any resistance or stiffness
options.D: Small amplitude of movement performed at the begining of range

questions.explanation: Grade II is a large-amplitude movement within the range, not meeting resistance.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Contraindication for manipulation is:
questions.explanation: Acute nerve root compression is a contraindication to manipulation.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Which of the following is contraindication for manual stretching?
questions.explanation: A bony block is a contraindication to stretching.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Manual therapies can be applied to:
questions.explanation: Manual therapy can be applied to joints, muscles and neural structures.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Exercise Therapy/Dina Gardiner/4th Ed./Pg. 135

questions.question: A therapist prepares to treat a patient with limited ankle range of motion using joint mobilization techniques. If the therapist elects to mobilize the talocrural joint in the resting position, the therapist should position the ankle in:

options.C: 10 degrees plantar flexion, midway between inversion and eversion

questions.explanation: The ankle resting position is about 10 degrees plantar flexion, midway between inversion and eversion.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist performs manual muscle test on a patient with unilateral upper extremity weakness. The patient is able to complete 75% of the available range of motion with gravity eliminated. The therapist should record the muscle grade as:
questions.explanation: Moving through 75% of range gravity-eliminated is grade 2 minus (poor minus).
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist performs a manual muscle test on a patient hip flexor. The therapist attempts to complete the test in supine, but the patient has difficulty holding the Exercise Therapy 31 limb in the test position. What alternate test position would be appropriate to test the patient's hip flexors?
questions.explanation: When supine is too hard, hip flexors can be tested in side-lying.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist completes a manual muscle test on the right lower trapezius muscle. In order to properly assess the muscle, the therapist should position the patient in:
questions.explanation: The lower trapezius is tested in prone.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist assesses the strength of a patient's right hip adductors by positioning the patient in right sidelying. During resting the patient is unable to move the extremity through the available range of motion. The most appropriate position to retest the hip adductors is:
questions.explanation: If the hip adductors cannot move in side-lying, retest supine.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A manual muscle test is conducted on the medial portion of the deltoid. The muscle is able to move through the full range of motion with gravity eliminated, but cannot function against gravity. The results of the manual muscle test should be recorded as:
questions.explanation: Full range gravity-eliminated is grade 2 (poor).
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist performs a manual muscle test on the primary hip abductor. The therapist should perform the test while palpating the:
questions.explanation: Gluteus medius is palpated while testing the main hip abductor.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A manual muscle test of the triceps reveals evidence of slight contractility without any active range of motion. The muscle should be graded as:
questions.explanation: A slight contraction without movement is grade 1 (trace).
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist records a manual muscle test grade of poor for right hip adduction. The most appropriate patient position to conduct the test would be:
questions.explanation: Grade 2 hip adduction is tested supine with gravity eliminated.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist performs a test to measure the strength of a patient's lower abdominal muscles. The most appropriate technique to examine the strength of the abdominals is:
questions.explanation: The double leg lowering test assesses lower abdominal strength.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist assigns a grade of good after completing a manual muscle test of the extensor digitorum. The most appropriate patient position to conduct the test would be:
questions.explanation: Extensor digitorum is tested in supine.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist completes a manual muscle test on a muscle that inverts the foot and assists in plantar flexion of the ankle joint. This description best describes the:
questions.explanation: Tibialis posterior inverts the foot and assists plantar flexion.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Muscles that flex or extend in the sagittal plane against gravity are tested in the ____________ plane for gravity eliminated testing?
questions.explanation: Gravity-eliminated testing is done in the horizontal (transverse) plane.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A patient is found to have limited knee extension. Which of the following mobilization techniques would be indicated?
questions.explanation: Limited knee extension is treated with anterior glide of the tibia.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist performs a manual muscle test on a patient's shoulder medial rotators. Which muscle would not be involved in this test?
questions.explanation: Teres minor is a lateral rotator, so it is not part of the medial rotator test.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Proper technique is essential to obtain accurate results when performing a manual muscle test. Which of the following manual muscle testing instructions is not accurate?

options.A: Have the patient perform the movement actively
options.C: Check the passive range of motion of the joint being moved
options.D: Apply pressure at the proximal end of the moving part

questions.explanation: Resistance should be applied at the distal end of the moving part.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist performs a manual muscle test on a patient with bilateral upper extremity weakness. The 32 therapist should test the patient's scapular adductors with the patient positioned in:
questions.explanation: Scapular adductors are tested in prone.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: To check peak muscle strength of the rectus femoris the patient should be placed in:
questions.explanation: Rectus femoris is tested in sitting with the hip flexed (sit lying).
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: The grade of muscle power in ankle dorsiflexors is zero in which of the following?

options.D: Absent visible or palpable muscle contraction

questions.explanation: Grade zero is no visible or palpable contraction.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: The best method to examine the grade 2 power of elbow flexors is:

options.D: Patient sitting with shoulder 90 degree abducted General Exercise

questions.explanation: Grade 2 elbow flexion is tested with the shoulder abducted 90 degrees to eliminate gravity.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A 16-year-old high school track participant returns to physical therapy after a physician appointment. The patient indicates that magnetic resonance imaging revealed a tear in the medial meniscus of the left knee. As you look back on the initial examination, which of the following special tests would you expect to have been position?
questions.explanation: McMurray's test is positive in meniscal tears.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A theraist performs goniometric measurements for elbow flexion with a patient in supine. In order to isolate elbow flexion the therapist should stabilize the:
questions.explanation: The distal humerus is stabilised when measuring elbow flexion.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: When measuring elbow flexion, the stationary arm of the goniometer should be aligned along the:
questions.explanation: The stationary arm is aligned with the humerus for elbow flexion.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Forearm supination is measured with the moving arm of the goniometer placed on the ________ side of the wrist?
questions.explanation: For supination the moving arm lies on the volar side of the wrist.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: When measuring hip abduction the stationary arm of the goniometer should be positioned __________?

options.A: Between the anterior superior iliac spines
options.B: Parallel to the anterior aspect of the femur Exercise Therapy 35
options.C: Along the midline of the tibia
options.D: Along a line from the crest of the ilium, femur, and greater trochanter

questions.explanation: For hip abduction the stationary arm lies between the anterior superior iliac spines.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist completes an upper extremity goniometric examination. The therapist records right elbow range of motion as 15-0-150 degrees. The total available range of motion for this patient is ______ degrees?
questions.explanation: Range 15-0-150 gives a total arc of 165 degrees.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: There are a variety of systems used to record goniometric measurements. Using the 0 to 180 system the anatomical position is used as the starting position for all movements except:
questions.explanation: Forearm rotation starts in mid-position, not the anatomical position, in the 0-180 system.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist performs goniometric measurements on a 38-year-old female rehabilitating from an acromioplasty. The therapist attempts on stabilize the scapula while measuring glenohumeral abduction. Failure to stabilize the scapula will led to:

options.A: Downward rotation and elevation of the scapula
options.B: Downward rotation and depression of the scapula
options.C: Upward rotation and elevation of the scapula
options.D: Upward rotation and depression of the scapula Taping

questions.explanation: Failure to stabilise the scapula allows upward rotation and depression of the scapula.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: When measurement ulnar deviation of the wrist, the moveable arm of the goniometer should be aligned with the:

options.A: Shaft of the second proximal phalanx
options.B: Shaft of the third proximal phalanx

questions.explanation: For wrist ulnar deviation the moving arm follows the second metacarpal.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist examines joint play movement by placing the joint in is resting position. This position is best described as:

options.A: Maximal congruency between the articular surfaces and the joint capsule
options.B: Minimal congruency between the articular surfaces and the joint capsule
options.C: Passive separation of the joint surfaces is limited
options.D: Parallel to the joint treatment plane.

questions.explanation: The resting position has minimal congruency and the capsule is most lax.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Joint Structure and Function/Norkin/3rd Ed./Pg. 77

questions.question: A physical therapist instructs a patient to move her lower teeth forward in relation to the upper teeth. This motion is termed:
questions.explanation: Moving the lower teeth forward is protrusion.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Orthopedic Physical Assessment/Magee/3rd Ed./Pg. 164

questions.question: Tests for the length of the hamstrings typically involve stabilization of the uninvolved leg while raising the leg to be tested. It is important to stabilize the uninvolved leg because it:

options.A: Prevents excessive posterior pelvic tilt and excessive flexion of the lumbar spine
options.B: Prevents excessive posterior pelvic tilt and excessive extension of the lumbar spine
options.C: Prevents excessive anterior pelvic tilt and excessive flexion of the lumbar spine
options.D: Prevents excessive anterior pelvic tilt and excessive extension of the lumbar spine

questions.explanation: Stabilising the opposite leg prevents posterior pelvic tilt and lumbar flexion.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Orthopedic Physical Assessment/David J. Magee/5th Ed./Pg. 698

questions.question: A patient exhibits pain and sensory loss in the posterior leg, calf, and dorsal foot. Extension of the hallux is poor, however the Achilles reflex is normal. What spinal level would you expect to be involved?
questions.explanation: Posterior leg and dorsal foot pain with weak hallux extension and a normal ankle jerk indicates L5.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Orthopedic Physical Assessment/Magee/3rd Ed./Pg. 369

questions.question: A sensory examination reveals light touch impairment to the buttock, thigh, and posterior leg the corresponding dermatome should be recorded as:
questions.explanation: Sensory loss over buttock, thigh and posterior leg is S1.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Orthopedic Physical Assessment/Magee/3rd Ed./Pg. 382

questions.question: A therapist utilizes resistive testing as part of an initial examination. To assess the C5 myotome the therapist should resist:
questions.explanation: Shoulder abduction tests the C5 myotome.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Orthopedic Physical Assessment/Magee/3rd Ed./Pg. 104

questions.question: A patient reports pain radiating down her posterior leg into the foot. She also exhibits weakness in plantar flexion and an absent Achilles reflex. Which spinal level would you expect to be involved?
questions.explanation: Posterior leg pain, weak plantar flexion and absent ankle jerk indicate S1-S2.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Orthopedic Physical Assessment/Magee/5th Ed./Pg. 550

questions.question: A therapist completes a sensory examination on a patient diagnosed with an incomplete spinal cord injury. To assess the C5 dermatome the therapist should examine the:

options.B: Superior portion of the chest above the axilla
options.D: Deltoid area of the lateral arm

questions.explanation: The C5 dermatome is the lateral arm over the deltoid.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Orthopedic Physical Assessment/Magee/5th Ed./Pg. 183

questions.question: A patient is positioned in supine with the hips flexed to 90 degrees and knees extended. As the patient slowly lowers her extended legs toward the horizontal, there is an increase in lordosis of the low back. This finding is indicative of weakness of the:
questions.explanation: Increased lordosis during double leg lowering indicates weak abdominals.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A physical therapist instructs a patient to reach behind her head and touch the superior medial angle of the opposite scapula. Which shoulder motions are necessary in order to follow this command?
questions.explanation: Touching the opposite scapula behind the head needs abduction and lateral rotation.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Orthopedic Physical Assessment/ David J. Magee/5th Ed./Pg. 255

questions.question: A therapist begins to suspect neurological involvement after completing an upper quarter screening examination. Which anatomic are would be most appropriate to gather information on the C8 dermatome?
questions.explanation: The C8 dermatome is the ulnar border of the hand.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Orthopedic Physical Assessment/Maggi/5th Ed./Pg. 159

questions.question: A therapist examines the elbow of a patient rehabilitating from a radial head fracture. Which of the following most accurately describes the close packed position of the radiohumeral joint? Biomechanics 57
questions.explanation: The radiohumeral joint is close-packed at 90 degrees flexion and 5 degrees supination.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Orthopedic Physical Assessment/Magee/5th Ed./Pg. 362

questions.question: A therapist completes a goniometric assessment of a patient's wrist. Assuming normal range of motion, which of the following motions would you expect to have the greatest available range?
questions.explanation: Wrist flexion has the greatest range.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Joint Structure and Function/Norkin/3rd Ed./Pg. 253

questions.question: A therapist measures passive forearm pronation and concludes the results are within normal limits. Which measurement would be classified as within normal limits?
questions.explanation: Normal pronation is about 80-90 degrees.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Joint Structure and Function/Norkin/3rd Ed./Pg. 234

questions.question: A therapist practices assessing joint end-feel. The therapist would most accurately classify normal elbow extension end-feel as:
questions.explanation: Elbow extension has a hard (bony) end-feel.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: A therapist attempts to palpate the lunate by moving his finger immediately distal to lister's tubercle. Which wrist motion with allow the therapist to facilitate palpation of the lunate?
questions.explanation: The lunate is palpated distal to Lister's tubercle with the wrist flexed.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Joint Structure Function/Norkin/3rd Ed./Pg. 252

questions.question: A therapist measures a patient's shoulder medial rotation with patient positioned in supine with glenohumeral joint in 90 degrees of abduction and the elbow in 90 degrees of flexion. The therapist records the patient's shoulder medial rotation is 0-70 degrees and classifies the end-feel as firm. Which portion of the joint capsule is primarily responsible for the firm end-feel?
questions.explanation: A firm end-feel limiting medial rotation implicates the posterior capsule.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Injury of median nerve at wrist is best detected by:

options.C: Loss of sensation of radial half of palm
options.D: Loss of sensation of tip of ring finger

questions.explanation: Abductor pollicis brevis best detects a median nerve injury at the wrist.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: To determine real leg length measurement is taken from:

options.A: ASIS to lateral malleolus on the same side
options.B: ASIS to the great toe on the same side
options.C: ASIS to the heel on the same side
options.D: ASIS to the medial malleolus of the leg

questions.explanation: True leg length is measured from the ASIS to the medial malleolus.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Essential Orthopedics/J Maheshwari/3rd Ed./Pg. 309

questions.question: All is correct about the true measurement of the limb except:

options.A: Length is measured after marking the bony points anterior superior iliac spine and medial malleolus
options.B: The pelvis should be made square
options.C: Length is measured keeping the limb in identical position
options.D: Measurement is taken from xiphisternum to medial malleolus

questions.explanation: Xiphisternum to medial malleolus is apparent, not true, leg length.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Due to paralysis or marked weakness of gluteus medius muscle the positive Trendelenburg's sign results into:

options.A: Dropping of pelvis on opposite side, i.e. left side
options.B: Dropping of pelvis on same side, i.e. right side
options.C: Flexion of hip and knee on same side, i.e. left side
options.D: Plantar flexion of right ankle to increase the leg length

questions.explanation: With a weak right gluteus medius the pelvis drops on the opposite (left) side.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Orthopedic Physical Assessment/Magee/3rd Ed./Pg. 690
